title: The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
one_line: The S&P 500 rose ~49 bps on average in the 24 hours before scheduled FOMC announcements (t > 4.5); since 1994 these windows earned ~80% of annual excess stock returns; holding the index only then had a Sharpe of ~1.1.

findings.statement: Average 49 bps in the 2pm-to-2pm window ending 15 minutes before the announcement.
Since 1994 about 80% of realized annual excess returns came in pre-FOMC windows (3.89%/yr vs 0.88% on other days).
No reversal afterwards; just-before-announcement to close ≈ 0.
Holding only in the window: Sharpe ~1.14 post-1994, 0.92 for 1980-2011.
European indices show 29-52 bps pre-FOMC returns; Nikkei none; nothing before other central banks.

why.pattern: Unexplained premium ahead of US monetary-policy news (risk reallocation / inattention partly).
why.mechanism: Authors find no single adequate explanation; volatility and liquidity declines explain only part.

reported_results.headline: ≈49 bps in 24h before FOMC; ~80% of excess returns since 1994.

tradable_edge: Long ES from 14:00 ET the day before a scheduled FOMC decision to 13:45 ET on decision day — but see Kurov et al. (2021): gone after 2015 except when uncertainty (VIX) is high.
angles: Condition on high volatility (AvgRange or VIX proxy) before the meeting

decay_risk.reason: Kurov, Wolfe & Gilbert (2021) show it disappeared for 2016-2019.

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 2), not by the weekly pipeline.
